thread:
jules: Heads up — customer ACME reporting intermittent 502s for hosted API since ~15:40 UTC. They see errors on batch scoring route /v1/generate when running large parallel jobs.
maria: any sample request ids or traces we can look at?
jules: sent a few: req=6f2a9b3e, req=6f2a9b3f, trace=tf-9a3c. Response body is basically 'upstream error' + early reset on streaming.
ingrid: looked at traces — envoy shows upstream reset: "upstream reset: reset reason=connection failure" around same timestamps. Auth proxy logs show repeated 504s to auth cluster.
alex: sounds like auth fanout is the common factor. We do per-item auth checks for batch items; if auth backend stalls, we get head-of-line blocking on the edge h2 stream.
jules: customer repro steps: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d @big_batch.json https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate  (they run 18 parallel clients). Payload per request ~2.1MB.
maria: can you paste the envoy log lines you have?
jules: pasted minimal snippet from edge logs:
```
[2026-03-17T15:40:12.123Z] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2" 502 NR - "curl/7.83" 0 0 0
upstream host:10.1.2.3:8443
upstream_reset_reason: connection failure
[2026-03-17T15:40:12.128Z] stream_id=4567 h2_stream_window_exceeded
```
alex: interesting — also correlating with h2_stream_window_exceeded counters on frontdoor. If auth returns large set-cookie/headers for billing, window drift can lead to resets.
ingrid: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce client concurrency (ask customer to drop to 6), 2) deploy temporary canary that batches auth checks server-side (remove per-item fanout), or 3) increase h2 window/flow-control on edge (riskier).
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-42 — paging oncall-sre.
maria: SRE, can you run a small load test that simulates 18 parallel clients with auth delayed by 200-500ms? Want to reproduce before making infra changes.
jules: customer agreed to try lower concurrency to 6 as a short-term workaround. They're available for tests this afternoon.
alex: follow-ups I'm opening: RB-1209 (add header-size / h2 window metrics), RB-1210 (proof-of-concept: server-side auth batching), RB-1211 (tunable h2 flow-control experiment).
maria: noted. Also capture billing auth response sizes in traces — looks like billing metadata sometimes adds ~3kB headers per sub-request.
ingrid: I'll run the synthetic with auth sleep and post traces here. If we see h2 window drift we can flip a small config.
jules: thanks team — I'll update customer with the workaround and next steps. :thumbsup:
